pathway.title: United Airlines Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity is the strongest support: cash and short-term investments of USD 14,653 million at 2026-09-30 and an undrawn revolver of USD 3.0 billion, raised to USD 5.0 billion on 2026-10-16 after the balance sheet date, sit against only USD 2,318 million of principal due over the next 15 months. Scale adds to it: FY2025 revenue of USD 59,070 million came from a hub network the company describes as the most comprehensive among North American carriers. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C16; calculation C18

Leverage fell sharply and has stalled: total debt to EBITDA went from 4.60x at FY2023 to 3.27x at FY2025 and is 3.31x for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, because 2026 aircraft borrowing outran repayments. Net leverage of 2.48x leans on net special credits and is 2.74x without them, against 2.49x at FY2025. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_ual-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C5

Underlying earnings have weakened more than reported earnings show: operating income before special items fell 22.37% to USD 2,790 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 while revenue rose 14.84%, and margin before special items fell from 8.23% to 5.56%. Fares recovered most of the cost increase, with unit revenue up 11.9% against unit cost up 12.5% as printed, but unit cost grew faster than unit revenue. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C16; calculation C17

Fuel is the first point of failure and is unhedged: it took 27.87% of nine-month operating expense against 21.00% a year earlier, with the price per gallon up 50.4% to USD 3.65. The company attributes the rise to 2026 Middle East conflicts and says it has historically had limited ability to raise fares and fees enough to offset a significant, rapid and sustained increase. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ual-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C15; calculation C17

Cash conversion is the weakest dimension: free cash flow was USD 2,557 million in FY2025 and USD 1,116 million over the twelve months, 14.01% of EBITDA against 33.42%, because capital expenditure of USD 7,044 million took 88.41% of EBITDA. Cash taxes have been small, with deferred tax 97.06% of FY2025 tax expense, so using up the loss carryforwards would lower cash flow further. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

Labor is the largest cost line and is repricing: salaries grew 8.28% in the nine months, 83% of employees are union-represented, and flight attendants ratified a five-year agreement in May 2026 with a USD 740 million payment. Several other groups were already open for amendment at the 2025 year end, so further resets are likely. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C15; calculation C18

Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2029 and market access is good but not investment grade: principal due in 2029 is USD 5,276 million, 22.82% of the printed total, and the revolver, term loan and 2029 senior secured notes share one collateral pool. Ratings are BB+ at S&P and Fitch and Ba1 at Moody's after three upgrades in 2025, with positive outlooks at two agencies, and the February 2026 notes priced at par. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C2

Financial policy is creditor-aligned so far: no dividend is paid, repurchases were USD 27 million in the nine months, no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed and the loyalty assets no longer secure debt, though USD 755 million of repurchase authorisation remains. That remainder is 67.65% of twelve-month free cash flow, so a resumption would matter. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C14

Customer prepayments are both a strength and a dependency: advance ticket sales and deferred loyalty revenue of USD 18,637 million are 1.27 times cash and short-term investments, so a fall in bookings would draw on liquidity before it shows in debt measures. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C13

cells.text: Hub-and-spoke network with hubs at Chicago, Denver, Houston, Los Angeles, Newark, San Francisco, Washington Dulles and Guam, serving six continents with the regional carriers
Scale supports origin-and-destination traffic, but one hub failure spreads across the network; Newark air traffic problems in 2025 and the late 2025 government shutdown forced schedule cuts
UAL is a holding company; United Airlines, Inc. supplies nearly 100% of revenues and expenses and approximately the entire balance of assets, liabilities and operating cash flow
Cash and operating claims sit in the subsidiary; holding company notes depend on the subsidiary guarantee
United Next plan: delivery of over 630 new narrow- and widebody aircraft by the end of 2034; mainline fleet of 1,066 aircraft with an average age of 15.3 years
Renewal lowers fuel use but sets a long capital and financing commitment

Regional capacity is about 6.1% of total capacity, bought from five carriers under capacity purchase agreements; United sets schedules and prices, owns the inventory risk and pays fuel and landing fees
Fixed-fee contracts add operating leverage: estimated future payments are USD 18.7 billion across the contract terms

MileagePlus earns miles from flights and partner purchases; the co-brand agreement with JPMorgan Chase is the main partner; partner agreements gave about USD 3.2 billion of FY2025 other operating revenue
Recurring non-ticket income that does not move with fuel; term and minimum commitments of the co-brand agreement are not stated
Member of Star Alliance; four passenger joint business arrangements and one cargo joint business with Lufthansa
Adds partner traffic and revenue; the amounts are not disclosed
Cargo revenue USD 1,779 million in FY2025 (3.01% of revenue); maintenance, flight academy and ground handling for third parties
Small diversifier; no profit by line is disclosed
Tickets sold through the website and app, travel agencies and online agencies; part of sales still uses legacy distribution that costs more
Third-quarter distribution expense rose 13.9% with passenger revenue, so cost follows price
No hedging of expected fuel use is planned; fuel was 21% of FY2025 operating expense and 27.87% in the nine months to 2026-09-30
Unhedged fuel is the largest swing cost and falls straight to margin
About 113,200 employees at 2025-12-31 and 117,900 at 2026-09-30, of whom 83% are represented by U.S. unions; agreements are under the Railway Labor Act and become amendable rather than expiring
Pay resets are recurring and cost-raising; flight attendants ratified in May 2026
Demand is higher in the second and third quarters; in 2025 the fourth quarter revenue exceeded both
Quarterly cash generation is uneven, so a single quarter is a weak guide to the year

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity: cash and short-term investments of USD 14,653 million and a revolver raised to USD 5.0 billion mean the company can fund a long period of weak free cash flow, and creditors are protected from a near-term liquidity event. The coverage of principal due through 2029 is 1.52 times with no free cash flow assumed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C18

The second strength is network scale and loyalty: a national hub network and the MileagePlus program with a bank co-brand agreement give recurring partner income of about USD 3.2 billion a year that does not move with fuel, which cushions cash flow against cycles. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C18

The third strength is deleveraging and market access: total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.60x to 3.31x, three agencies upgraded the company in 2025, and the 2026 notes priced at par, which lowers refinancing risk for the 2029 principal. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C5

The fourth strength is pricing power in a strong demand year: unit revenue rose 11.9% on capacity up 2.7%, which shows fares can move with costs when demand is firm, though it is not contractual. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C17

The fifth strength is conservative financial policy: no dividend, small repurchases and no controlling holder mean value is not being extracted ahead of creditors, which keeps the downside driven by operations rather than owner choices. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66

The first weakness is unhedged fuel: fuel took 27.87% of nine-month operating expense with the price per gallon up 50.4%, and without a hedge or a stated pass-through any further rise falls directly to margin and free cash flow, which is the first break in the downside path. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C15; calculation C17

The second weakness is cash conversion: free cash flow fell to USD 1,116 million over twelve months with capital expenditure at 88.41% of EBITDA, so deleveraging now depends on EBITDA growth because internal cash is largely absorbed by aircraft. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C6; calculation C7

The third weakness is labor: salaries rose 8.28% in the nine months and further agreements are open, so wage resets raise the fixed cost base permanently and reduce margin protection when demand softens. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C15

The fourth weakness is the maturity and collateral structure: 22.82% of printed principal falls due in 2029 and the best collateral is shared among the revolver, term loan and secured notes, so unsecured creditors depend on residual value and on market access at refinancing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C2

The fifth weakness is earnings quality and dependence on customer float: net special credits of USD 756 million raise reported EBITDA and hide 2.74x net leverage behind 2.48x, and float of USD 18,637 million is 1.27 times liquidity, so a bookings shock would hit liquidity before leverage. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C5; calculation C13

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The 2026 financing was a refinancing plus aircraft borrowing, not a shareholder distribution: on 2026-02-02 and 2026-02-06 the holding company issued USD 1,000 million each of senior notes due 2031 and 2029, both at par and guaranteed by the operating subsidiary, and on 2026-02-24 the operating subsidiary redeemed all USD 2,000 million of its senior secured notes due 2026. The filings do not state whether the new notes are secured or how they rank against the term loan and the secured notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ual-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76

The term loan was repriced on 2026-02-03 by Amendment No. 4, which cut the margin from 2.00% to 1.75% on Term SOFR loans and from 1.00% to 0.75% on other market-rate loans; the filings state no consideration given for the change. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 the operating subsidiary also borrowed USD 4.6 billion secured on aircraft, maturing between 2029 and 2038 at Term SOFR plus an average margin of 1.4%, and made USD 4.9 billion of debt payments, including a USD 0.6 billion partial prepayment on 2026-06-23 of the USD 1.5 billion Treasury payroll support note due 2030. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

After the latest balance sheet, on 2026-10-16, the revolving credit facility was amended and restated: commitments rose from USD 3.0 billion to USD 5.0 billion, maturity moved from 2029-02-15 to 2031-10-16 and the margins were lowered, with no borrowing outstanding at the date of the report. The facility is secured by route authorities, slots and terminal rights that also secure the term loan and the 2029 senior secured notes, and its lenders may require prepayment if a change of control occurs and the lender accepts a change of control offer. Figures at 2026-09-30 in this review do not include it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39

No purchase of an operating business and no sponsor transaction is described in the filings read. The equity-type transactions were investments: financial contributions to the merger of Mesa and Republic completed on 2025-11-25, whose amount is not stated, in exchange for 2,744,348 additional Republic shares received on 2026-02-03, and a USD 100 million subscription for Azul depositary shares agreed on 2026-02-17 that left United with 8.6% of Azul at 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.value: Financial foundation for United Airlines Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the consolidated holding-company statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, carrying-value debt, liquidity, derived EBITDA and a last-twelve-months build, with the 2026-10-16 revolving credit facility amendment shown as a subsequent event.

EBITDA is derived because the issuer states none, and it includes net special credits of USD 756 million.

The share repurchase authorisation had USD 755 million remaining as of 2026-10-15 with no repurchases in the third quarter. The amended facility requires unrestricted liquidity of at least USD 2,000 million and a collateral coverage ratio of at least 1.6 to 1.0. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell sharply and has since stopped improving. Total debt at carrying value dropped from USD 31,660 million at FY2023 to USD 24,988 million at FY2025 while derived EBITDA rose from USD 6,882 million to USD 7,652 million, taking total debt to EBITDA from 4.60x to 3.27x. Since then debt has risen to USD 26,398 million as aircraft financings of 4.6 billion outran repayments, and total debt to EBITDA is 3.31x for the twelve months to 2026-09-30. Net debt to EBITDA of 2.48x looks level with FY2025 at 2.49x, but the last twelve months include net special credits of USD 756 million, which reflect aircraft sale-leaseback gains recorded in 2026, and without them net leverage is 2.74x against 2.41x. For creditors, the improvement came mainly from repaying debt, with payments of long-term debt, finance leases and other financial liabilities of USD 10,138 million in FY2024 and USD 4,771 million in FY2025 against issuance of USD 6,139 million and USD 578 million, and the next test is whether earnings carry the added fleet debt without special credits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover strengthened as expensive debt was repaid. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.72 times in FY2023, 5.37 times in FY2024 and 5.75 times in FY2025, while interest expense fell from USD 1,956 million to USD 1,373 million. The last twelve months cash figure cannot be built because the quarterly reports omit cash paid for interest, so the accrued-expense cover of 5.88 times is shown as a proxy only. The strongest contrary reading is that new aircraft debt at floating rates, about 1.4% above the benchmark, adds interest that the earlier years did not carry; interest expense for the nine months already ran at USD 1,029 million against USD 1,048 million a year earlier, so the effect is not yet visible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion has weakened. Free cash flow, operating cash flow less capital expenditure, was USD 3,830 million in FY2024 and USD 2,557 million in FY2025, and USD 1,116 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, or 0.14 of EBITDA against 0.33 in FY2025. Capital expenditure rose to USD 7,044 million over the latest twelve months from USD 5,874 million as aircraft deliveries continued, and operating cash flow was held back by a one-off flight attendant ratification payment. The mechanism is that fleet investment is outrunning internally generated cash and being met with new secured debt, which raises leverage unless EBITDA grows with it.

fields.value: Liquidity is ample against near-term maturities but depends on customer-funded float. Cash and short-term investments were USD 14,653 million at 2026-09-30 and the undrawn revolver USD 3,000 million, against USD 1,848 million of current debt and USD 934 million of current operating leases. Advance ticket sales of USD 10,672 million and frequent flyer deferred revenue of USD 7,965 million are a non-debt funding source of USD 18,637 million that exceeds the liquidity pool; a fall in bookings would draw that float down before it shows in debt metrics. The ladder shows USD 5,276 million of principal due in 2029, the largest single year before 2030, which is the refinancing point to watch.

fields.value: Three definitions of debt and two of cash are in play and each serves one purpose. The balance-sheet captions, USD 26,398 million, serve leverage because they carry finance leases and other financial liabilities; the debt note carrying value of USD 22,964 million and principal of USD 23,116 million serve the maturity ladder and the reconciliation; and the issuer total of USD 34.3 billion adds operating leases and serves its own fixed-obligation disclosure. Net debt deducts cash and cash equivalents only, USD 6,648 million; the issuer counts short-term investments as well, and doing so lowers net leverage to 1.47x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership and governance review of United Airlines Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the operating model, ownership and control, capital allocation and sponsor-type behaviour, the 2026 financing and investment transactions and the dated event history, read from the five supplied filings and the source readiness review, with no external sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: United's credit risk is operating, not owner-driven: no controlling holder is disclosed, no dividend is paid and the loyalty business carries no secured debt, so creditors bear airline-cycle and fuel risk rather than extraction risk. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 fuel expense rose USD 4,520 million (53.35%) and operating income before special items fell 22.37% to USD 2,790 million, while reported operating income rose only because of USD 749 million of special credits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit case therefore rests on pricing power against fuel and labor costs and on aircraft financing, because the revolver, the term loan and the 2029 senior secured notes share one collateral pool of route authorities, slots and terminal rights, and capital spending is rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership creates no identified sponsor risk: the shares are listed on Nasdaq, no holder is identified as controlling, the Treasury warrants issued in the pandemic were all exercised by March 2025, and the only other equity security outstanding is two junior preferred shares whose rights the filings read do not describe. The tax benefits preservation plan that deters any buyer from crossing 4.9% of the shares expires on 2026-12-04, after the as-of date, and the filings do not say it will be renewed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a scale network carrier with diversified geography but one core product: passenger revenue was 90.47% of FY2025 revenue and domestic revenue 59.28%, so earnings follow U.S. air travel demand and fares more than any second business. Cargo was 3.01% and other operating revenue 6.52%, most of it loyalty partner income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Loyalty is a real strength and prepayments are a real obligation: partner agreements, led by the co-brand card with JPMorgan Chase, produced about USD 3.2 billion of FY2025 revenue and grew 12.50% in the nine months to USD 2.7 billion, and no debt is now secured on the loyalty assets. Against that, customer prepayments of USD 18,637 million are 1.27x cash and short-term investments of USD 14,653 million, so a drop in bookings or a processor demand for reserves would reach liquidity quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 138; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fuel is the largest swing cost and is not hedged: it took 27.87% of nine-month operating expense against 21.00% a year earlier, at an average USD 3.65 per gallon against USD 2.43, the company does not hedge fuel and the filings give no price sensitivity. Fares have recovered much of it, with total revenue per seat mile up 11.9% on capacity up only 2.7%, but operating margin before special items still fell from 8.23% to 5.56%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C6; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Labor is the largest cost line and is repricing upward: 83% of employees are represented by unions, salaries and related costs grew 8.28% in the nine months, and flight attendants ratified a five-year agreement in May 2026 with a USD 740 million ratification payment on 2026-09-15. The annual report also lists several other groups whose agreements were already open for amendment and states that negotiations are active with all of them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ual-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder distributions have been modest and creditor-aligned so far: no dividend is paid, repurchases of USD 637 million in FY2025 were 24.91% of free cash flow and fell to USD 27 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the MileagePlus debt was repaid in 2024 and 2025. In 2026 the direction on debt reversed, with nine-month borrowing of USD 6,698 million above repayments of USD 5,541 million to fund aircraft.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C14; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is the main call on cash: nine-month capital expenditure rose 29.37% to USD 5,154 million, nine-month free cash flow fell to USD 1,720 million from USD 3,161 million, and the annual report guides 2026 adjusted capital expenditure to less than USD 8.0 billion because of aircraft delivery delays. The firm order book that runs to 2034 fell by 82 aircraft over three quarters, so the commitment is long and largely contractual.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party exposure is small against the business but structural: United holds minority stakes in the regional carriers that fly under its capacity contracts, pays them about USD 1.1 billion a year, and committed financial contributions, whose amount is not stated, to the 2025 merger of Mesa and Republic in return for an additional stake that took its holding in Republic to about 22%. These contracts are described as ordinary-course and are not shown to leak value to a shareholder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is sound: the auditor issued unqualified opinions on the statements and on internal control over financial reporting, the single critical audit matter concerns the China route authority intangible asset, and disclosure controls were concluded effective at 2026-09-30. Reporting follows the quarterly cycle with no restatement or waiver described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The shared collateral pool is the main structural point for unsecured creditors: route authorities, slots and terminal rights secure the revolver, the term loan and the 2029 senior secured notes on a shared senior basis, a substantial part of the aircraft is also pledged, and the revolver was enlarged from USD 3.0 billion to USD 5.0 billion on 2026-10-16, after the latest balance sheet. Owned aircraft are 89.87% of the mainline fleet, but owned does not mean unencumbered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a benign view is the cost trend: reported nine-month operating income rose 6.4% only because of USD 749 million of special credits, mostly gains on aircraft sale-leasebacks, while the underlying measure fell 22.37% and the third-quarter margin slipped to 8.09% from 9.16%. A further fuel rise that fares cannot recover, or a demand slowdown with the same cost base, would cut free cash flow that already fell in 2026, and the unhedged position gives creditors no buffer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view that owner behaviour is not a risk would change if a holder crossed 5% after the preservation plan lapses, if repurchases resumed at the FY2025 pace while capital spending rises, if secured debt were again raised on the loyalty assets, or if the revolver were drawn for distributions. The remaining USD 755 million repurchase authorisation and the loyalty assets that no longer secure debt show the capacity exists, though use of either is not yet documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, independence, committee structure and holders above 5% are not established; the conclusion that no holder controls the company rests on the filings naming none, and a large holder or voting arrangement would overturn it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreements and indentures are not supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, add secured debt or move assets cannot be measured; the low governance risk rests on documented behaviour and would be reassessed once the covenant package is read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings report one segment and give no customer, route or hub profitability, so the claim that revenue is diversified rests on the split by region and by revenue type alone and hub concentration cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings describe no fuel hedge and give no price sensitivity, so the estimate that fares have recovered much of the fuel increase rests on nine-month unit revenue changes and not on a stated pass-through, and it could reverse if demand softens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loyalty partner income is disclosed only as rounded totals with no split of the co-brand card agreement, its term or minimum commitments, so the durability of the largest non-ticket income and the financing value of the loyalty assets that no longer secure debt are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 financing was a refinancing plus aircraft borrowing, not a shareholder distribution: on 2026-02-02 and 2026-02-06 the holding company issued USD 1,000 million each of senior notes due 2031 and 2029, both at par and guaranteed by the operating subsidiary, and on 2026-02-24 the operating subsidiary redeemed all USD 2,000 million of its senior secured notes due 2026. The filings do not state whether the new notes are secured or how they rank against the term loan and the secured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The term loan was repriced on 2026-02-03 by Amendment No. 4, which cut the margin from 2.00% to 1.75% on Term SOFR loans and from 1.00% to 0.75% on other market-rate loans; the filings state no consideration given for the change. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 the operating subsidiary also borrowed USD 4.6 billion secured on aircraft, maturing between 2029 and 2038 at Term SOFR plus an average margin of 1.4%, and made USD 4.9 billion of debt payments, including a USD 0.6 billion partial prepayment on 2026-06-23 of the USD 1.5 billion Treasury payroll support note due 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the latest balance sheet, on 2026-10-16, the revolving credit facility was amended and restated: commitments rose from USD 3.0 billion to USD 5.0 billion, maturity moved from 2029-02-15 to 2031-10-16 and the margins were lowered, with no borrowing outstanding at the date of the report. The facility is secured by route authorities, slots and terminal rights that also secure the term loan and the 2029 senior secured notes, and its lenders may require prepayment if a change of control occurs and the lender accepts a change of control offer. Figures at 2026-09-30 in this review do not include it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No purchase of an operating business and no sponsor transaction is described in the filings read. The equity-type transactions were investments: financial contributions to the merger of Mesa and Republic completed on 2025-11-25, whose amount is not stated, in exchange for 2,744,348 additional Republic shares received on 2026-02-03, and a USD 100 million subscription for Azul depositary shares agreed on 2026-02-17 that left United with 8.6% of Azul at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Low. The level is driven by the absence of a controlling holder, no dividends and modest repurchases, because no owner channel exists through which value can leave the credit, which implies that creditors face operating and fuel risk rather than extraction risk. Countervailing evidence is the unexamined legal capacity under the debt documents, the remaining repurchase authorisation and the expiry of the preservation plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each gap names what is missing, the search made and what it limits. Severity is stated for the credit snapshot objective of this run; the same gap can be more serious for modules this run does not include.

fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis of United Airlines Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, financial profile, downside path and monitoring for the holding company group, drawn from the five supplied filings and the three earlier analyses, with no external sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: United's credit profile is sound but no longer improving: scale, liquidity and lower debt support creditors, while an unhedged fuel shock, higher labor cost and heavy aircraft spending have cut margin and free cash flow, so risk lies in cash conversion, not liquidity. Total debt is 3.31x EBITDA and net debt 2.48x, or 2.74x without special credits, and free cash flow fell to USD 1,116 million over twelve months. Cash and short-term investments of USD 14,653 million cover principal due through 2029 1.52 times with no free cash flow, so the main downside is fuel staying above fares until the 2029 maturities must be refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the strongest support: cash and short-term investments of USD 14,653 million at 2026-09-30 and an undrawn revolver of USD 3.0 billion, raised to USD 5.0 billion on 2026-10-16 after the balance sheet date, sit against only USD 2,318 million of principal due over the next 15 months. Scale adds to it: FY2025 revenue of USD 59,070 million came from a hub network the company describes as the most comprehensive among North American carriers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C16; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell sharply and has stalled: total debt to EBITDA went from 4.60x at FY2023 to 3.27x at FY2025 and is 3.31x for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, because 2026 aircraft borrowing outran repayments. Net leverage of 2.48x leans on net special credits and is 2.74x without them, against 2.49x at FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_ual-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying earnings have weakened more than reported earnings show: operating income before special items fell 22.37% to USD 2,790 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 while revenue rose 14.84%, and margin before special items fell from 8.23% to 5.56%. Fares recovered most of the cost increase, with unit revenue up 11.9% against unit cost up 12.5% as printed, but unit cost grew faster than unit revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C16; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fuel is the first point of failure and is unhedged: it took 27.87% of nine-month operating expense against 21.00% a year earlier, with the price per gallon up 50.4% to USD 3.65. The company attributes the rise to 2026 Middle East conflicts and says it has historically had limited ability to raise fares and fees enough to offset a significant, rapid and sustained increase.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ual-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C15; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is the weakest dimension: free cash flow was USD 2,557 million in FY2025 and USD 1,116 million over the twelve months, 14.01% of EBITDA against 33.42%, because capital expenditure of USD 7,044 million took 88.41% of EBITDA. Cash taxes have been small, with deferred tax 97.06% of FY2025 tax expense, so using up the loss carryforwards would lower cash flow further.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Labor is the largest cost line and is repricing: salaries grew 8.28% in the nine months, 83% of employees are union-represented, and flight attendants ratified a five-year agreement in May 2026 with a USD 740 million payment. Several other groups were already open for amendment at the 2025 year end, so further resets are likely.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C15; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2029 and market access is good but not investment grade: principal due in 2029 is USD 5,276 million, 22.82% of the printed total, and the revolver, term loan and 2029 senior secured notes share one collateral pool. Ratings are BB+ at S&P and Fitch and Ba1 at Moody's after three upgrades in 2025, with positive outlooks at two agencies, and the February 2026 notes priced at par.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is creditor-aligned so far: no dividend is paid, repurchases were USD 27 million in the nine months, no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed and the loyalty assets no longer secure debt, though USD 755 million of repurchase authorisation remains. That remainder is 67.65% of twelve-month free cash flow, so a resumption would matter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer prepayments are both a strength and a dependency: advance ticket sales and deferred loyalty revenue of USD 18,637 million are 1.27 times cash and short-term investments, so a fall in bookings would draw on liquidity before it shows in debt measures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is pricing power: revenue rose 14.84% on capacity growth of 2.7%, unit revenue rose 11.9%, management states that its long-term outlook is positive because it expects demand to stay strong, and three agencies upgraded the company in 2025. If fuel falls back toward the USD 2.43 a gallon of the prior-year nine months while fares hold, the underlying margin would recover quickly because fuel is the swing cost, and the view would move to stable or improving.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C16; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if margin before special items stayed below the nine-month level of 5.56%, if twelve-month free cash flow turned negative as it did in FY2023, or if repurchases resumed while capital spending stayed high. A drawing on the revolver for operating needs, or a rating outlook change to negative, would confirm that the downside path described later had begun.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer filings, rating agency reports or market prices are supplied, so the judgement that the business profile is stronger than the leverage profile is not benchmarked against comparable airlines, and the rating trajectory rests on the company's own statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside arithmetic holds volume, prices and all other costs at latest levels and ignores fare, capacity and capital spending responses, so it measures exposure and is not a forecast; a faster response would shrink the cash burn shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maturity coverage uses the principal ladder for long-term debt agreements only, which excludes finance leases and other financial liabilities and any payments on them, so the coverage of principal due through 2029 is overstated by an amount that is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No forward model or management plan beyond the 2026 capital expenditure guidance is supplied, so the outlook and the timing of the 2029 refinancing are read from disclosed commitments and not from projected cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status is ready with limitations: all five filings and the three earlier analyses are available and agree on entity, period and perimeter, but peers, rating agency reports, debt documents and a forward model are not supplied, which bounds the benchmarking, recovery and forward conclusions rather than the findings drawn here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: United is a hub-based network airline whose cash flow depends on passenger revenue, which was 90.47% of FY2025 revenue, with 59.28% earned in the domestic market and 40.72% in Atlantic, Pacific and Latin American markets. Cargo, loyalty partner income and ancillary fees add diversification of source but not of cycle, so earnings follow U.S. air travel demand, fares and fuel; tickets are sold at most twelve months ahead, so revenue visibility is short and the credit rests on liquidity and network scale rather than on contracted revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; calculation C16; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strategic shift that matters for creditors is the United Next fleet plan, which commits the company to several hundred new aircraft by 2034 and to the financing that goes with them, while the 2025 and 2026 history is one of debt repayment, a larger regional supplier merger and a labor reset. The model supports debt service through scale and customer prepayments, and it weakens refinancing confidence only if fuel and labor costs outrun fares for longer than liquidity can bridge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: United Airlines Holdings, Inc. is a holding company whose wholly owned subsidiary United Airlines, Inc. supplies nearly all revenue, expenses, assets and operating cash flow, so the holding company notes rely on the subsidiary guarantee and the subsidiary's assets are the real credit support. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, no dividend is paid and repurchases were small, and Business & governance assesses sponsor and governance risk as low on documented behaviour alone, because the debt documents and the proxy statement are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and discretionary but currently price-led: nine-month capacity rose 2.7% while unit revenue rose 11.9%, and revenue grew 14.84%, so yield and fees, not volume, carried the increase. Management states that it has historically had limited ability to raise fares and fees enough to offset a large, fast and sustained fuel increase, and that air travel demand follows economic strength, so the 2026 pricing gain is evidence of present demand, not a contractual floor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C16; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ancillary fees of USD 4.8 billion and loyalty partner income of about USD 3.2 billion in FY2025 add recurring items that do not move one for one with fuel, and customer prepayments of USD 18,637 million fund operations, but that float grew by USD 906 million in FY2025 operating cash flow, 10.75% of the total, and would reverse if bookings fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C13; calculation C18; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are largely fixed in the short run: labor and fuel together are 53.43% of FY2025 operating expense, regional carriers are paid fixed-fee rates with USD 18.7 billion of estimated future payments, and firm aircraft orders carry material liabilities if modified. Margin can be defended only through fares and capacity: unit revenue less unit cost before special items fell 24.39% in the nine months, so cost inflation has so far outrun pricing at the margin even though revenue per seat mile rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C10; calculation C15; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Flexibility exists in capacity, which management used in 2026 by cutting lower-margin capacity, and delivery delays have held adjusted capital expenditure for 2026 below USD 8.0 billion, but labor agreements, regional contracts and the order book do not shrink quickly. The nine-month operating margin before special items fell to 5.56% from 8.23%, so margins cannot be defended against a further fuel or wage shock without a fare response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C9; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts weakly into free cash flow because capital intensity is high: capital expenditure over the twelve months was USD 7,044 million, 88.41% of EBITDA, nine-month spending rose 29.37%, and free cash flow was 14.01% of EBITDA against 33.42% in FY2025. Most of the spending is growth and renewal capital under firm orders that run to 2034, so it can be slowed by delivery delays but not cancelled without cost, and it is increasingly financed with new secured aircraft debt, which raises leverage unless EBITDA grows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash taxes have flattered free cash flow: deferred tax was 97.06% of FY2025 tax expense and the federal loss carryforwards of about USD 2.2 billion tax-effected equal 2.38 years of that deferred charge, so cash taxes will rise as the losses are used up. Cash interest is not printed for the interim periods, and interest expense covers EBITDA 5.88 times as a proxy, with at least USD 11,800 million of floating-rate principal, 51.05% of the printed total, adding about USD 118 million a year of interest per percentage point of rate change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C8; calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and pressures margin: the industry competes on routes, fares, capacity and loyalty, consolidation and immunized joint businesses reshape competitors, and the company states that it often has to match discounted fares to keep traffic. That limits the pass-through of cost increases and is why a fuel shock lands on margin first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is moderate: any fit U.S. carrier may fly domestic routes, but slots, gates and airport infrastructure at the hubs are constrained, and the company's route authorities, slots and terminal rights are collateral for its secured debt, which supports their value to lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes matter for short-haul and business travel: surface travel replaces short flights and videoconferencing replaces trips when conditions weaken, so a fall in business and premium travel would hit revenue first, which raises the cyclicality of cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is limited for consumers individually but real in aggregate: tickets are sold through the company's own channels and through agencies and online agencies, a legacy distribution cost remains, and the largest partner income depends on one co-brand card agreement whose terms are not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is high: substantially all aircraft and engines come from Boeing and Airbus and a limited number of engine suppliers, delivery delays and tariffs can raise cost or force older aircraft to stay in service, and the labor force is largely unionized under the Railway Labor Act, so suppliers and unions both set cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material: the FAA can restrict capacity at hubs, a federal government shutdown forced schedule cuts at about 40 airports in late 2025, tariffs on aircraft and parts could raise fleet cost, and labor agreements are negotiated under federal law with open amendable dates. Each of these acts on revenue or cost without any offset in the company's control, so they raise the volatility of cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic factors are the dominant driver: fuel prices rose with Middle East conflicts in 2026, demand follows economic strength, and floating-rate debt ties interest cost to market rates. Social and technological factors, such as customer service performance and system outages, are not primary credit drivers on the materials supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strengths are liquidity and committed facilities that cover principal due through 2029, a hub network with scale and loyalty income that does not move with fuel, lower debt than at FY2023 with rating upgrades in 2025, and loyalty assets that no longer secure debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaknesses are unhedged fuel exposure, weak and falling free cash flow after heavy capital spending, labor cost that resets upward under union contracts, and a shared collateral pool that makes secured debt the first claim on the best assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The opportunities that could improve credit quality are a fall in fuel prices with fares held, which would restore the margin, and a further rating upgrade toward investment grade, which two agencies' positive outlooks leave open and which would cut funding cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threats are a sustained fuel price, capacity limits from regulators or a government shutdown, aircraft delivery delays or tariff-driven cost increases, and repurchases or investments resuming while free cash flow is low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity: cash and short-term investments of USD 14,653 million and a revolver raised to USD 5.0 billion mean the company can fund a long period of weak free cash flow, and creditors are protected from a near-term liquidity event. The coverage of principal due through 2029 is 1.52 times with no free cash flow assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is network scale and loyalty: a national hub network and the MileagePlus program with a bank co-brand agreement give recurring partner income of about USD 3.2 billion a year that does not move with fuel, which cushions cash flow against cycles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is deleveraging and market access: total debt to EBITDA fell from 4.60x to 3.31x, three agencies upgraded the company in 2025, and the 2026 notes priced at par, which lowers refinancing risk for the 2029 principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is pricing power in a strong demand year: unit revenue rose 11.9% on capacity up 2.7%, which shows fares can move with costs when demand is firm, though it is not contractual.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth strength is conservative financial policy: no dividend, small repurchases and no controlling holder mean value is not being extracted ahead of creditors, which keeps the downside driven by operations rather than owner choices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is unhedged fuel: fuel took 27.87% of nine-month operating expense with the price per gallon up 50.4%, and without a hedge or a stated pass-through any further rise falls directly to margin and free cash flow, which is the first break in the downside path.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C15; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is cash conversion: free cash flow fell to USD 1,116 million over twelve months with capital expenditure at 88.41% of EBITDA, so deleveraging now depends on EBITDA growth because internal cash is largely absorbed by aircraft.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is labor: salaries rose 8.28% in the nine months and further agreements are open, so wage resets raise the fixed cost base permanently and reduce margin protection when demand softens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is the maturity and collateral structure: 22.82% of printed principal falls due in 2029 and the best collateral is shared among the revolver, term loan and secured notes, so unsecured creditors depend on residual value and on market access at refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is earnings quality and dependence on customer float: net special credits of USD 756 million raise reported EBITDA and hide 2.74x net leverage behind 2.48x, and float of USD 18,637 million is 1.27 times liquidity, so a bookings shock would hit liquidity before leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C5; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are strong, supported by revenue of USD 59,070 million and the most comprehensive route network among North American carriers as the company describes it, while competitive advantage is average because network and loyalty are offset by industry rivalry, and business diversification is average because passenger revenue is over 90% of the total even though regions are spread.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is weak to average and margin stability weak, because labor, regional and aircraft commitments are rigid and margin before special items fell to 5.56%; free cash flow stability is weak, at 14.01% of EBITDA over the twelve months. Ability to refinance is average to strong, given BB+ and Ba1 ratings with positive outlooks and par pricing in 2026, and liquidity position is strong; financial policy and governance is average to strong, with no sponsor and modest distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-03-31_ual-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C6; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity, scale and lower leverage; the main constraints are fuel, cash conversion and the 2029 concentration; the trend is flat leverage with weaker underlying earnings. Key missing datapoints are the debt documents, the covenant coverage figures and peer comparisons, so the profile against typical leveraged-credit airlines is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the headwinds are fuel at or above the third-quarter level of USD 3.90 a gallon, labor resets under agreements still open, and aircraft financing that adds debt, while the tailwinds are strong demand that management expects to persist, a revolver raised to USD 5.0 billion that extends to 2031, and principal due of only USD 2,318 million over the next 15 months. Free cash flow is the observable that decides whether leverage resumes falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C2; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the commitment is the fleet: deliveries run to 2034, the 2029 principal of USD 5,276 million is the largest single year before 2030, and federal loss carryforwards are being used up, so cash taxes will rise. Newer aircraft should lower fuel use per seat, which would improve the fuel exposure, but only if the order book is financed without lifting debt faster than EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_ual-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C2; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is fuel staying at the third-quarter price of USD 3.90 a gallon for a further twelve months while fare gains stall, which on twelve-month volume adds USD 2,531 million of fuel expense, 31.77% of EBITDA. The first operational break is margin: EBITDA would fall to about USD 5,436 million, free cash flow would turn to a burn of USD 1,415 million, and total debt to EBITDA would rise to 4.86x with debt unchanged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity absorbs it comfortably over a year, with cash and short-term investments covering the burn and the next 15 months of principal 3.93 times, and the amended revolver, a subsequent event, adds committed capacity of USD 5.0 billion that the ratio does not count. The pressure point is the refinancing: over three years the same burn plus principal due through 2029 would use almost all cash, 1.06 times covered, so resilience then depends on refinancing the 2029 principal, on market access at BB+ and Ba1, and on management levers such as capacity cuts, fare and fee increases, the timing of capital spending and no repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ual-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation C4; calculation C21; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a prolonged fuel price above fares and rising labor cost that turns free cash flow negative and lifts leverage ahead of the 2029 maturities, with the shared collateral pool leaving unsecured creditors exposed if market access closes. The scenario is arithmetic exposure, not a forecast, and it does not assume default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C20; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, United Airlines Holdings, Inc. presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, liquidity, lower debt and a loyalty income stream, but credit quality is constrained by unhedged fuel, high capital intensity and rising labor cost. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to weak because free cash flow fell to USD 1,116 million over twelve months and underlying margin has fallen. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on liquidity, the extended revolver, positive rating momentum and market access for the 2029 principal. The primary downside path is fuel staying above fares while labor and aircraft costs keep rising. Further analysis would require the debt documents, covenant coverage figures, peer comparisons and a forward model. Fundamental credit synthesis completed. Top risk: unhedged fuel cost against fares, feeding weak free cash flow ahead of the 2029 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each gap names what is missing, the search made and what it limits. Severity is stated for the credit snapshot objective of this run; the same gap can be more serious for modules this run does not include.
